newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end higher in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end higher in dull trade.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures ended higher on position squaring after extremely thin trade on Friday, amid uncertainties over the dollar's direction ahead of U.S. job data later today, traders said.
"People were sidelined amid uncertainties ahead of U.S. job data," said one trader. "Though aluminium prices rose on the LME back to $1,600, the climb was seen driven mainly by technical factors."
Traders ascribed today's advance to position squaring ahead of weekend.
Many individual investors shifted attention to precious metals markets where platinum and palladium fluctuated widely, they added.
Estimated trade volume dropped to 822 lots, the lowest since the market was launched in April.
TOCOM benchmark April 1998 added 1.2 yen to stand at 192.5 yen per kg, while others gained between 0.7 yen and 1.1 yen.

The dollar was trading below 116 yen in late Asia amid concerns over Japan's trade surplus with the United States after a Japanese newspaper reported that the Denver summit later this month will take up the question of Japan's trade surplus. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-6179
